notes.heading: Overview
points: India is known as a land of diverse festivals reflecting its cultural, religious, and regional diversity
Fairs and festivals are deeply connected with agriculture, seasons, religion, and social traditions
They promote unity in diversity and cultural exchange
Festivals can be religious, seasonal, tribal, or national
Fairs often combine trade, pilgrimage, and cultural performances

notes.heading: Classification of Festivals
points: Religious festivals – based on Hinduism, Islam, Christianity, Sikhism, Buddhism, Jainism, etc.
Seasonal festivals – linked to harvest and agricultural cycles
Tribal festivals – unique to indigenous communities
National festivals – celebrated across India (Independence Day, Republic Day, Gandhi Jayanti)
Cultural fairs – mix of trade, culture, and rituals

notes.heading: Hindu Festivals
points: Diwali – festival of lights symbolizing victory of good over evil
Holi – festival of colors celebrating spring and divine love
Navratri/Durga Puja – worship of Goddess Durga
Makar Sankranti – harvest festival marking sun’s transition
Raksha Bandhan – celebration of sibling bond

notes.heading: Islamic Festivals
points: Eid-ul-Fitr – marks end of Ramadan fasting
Eid-ul-Adha – commemorates sacrifice of Prophet Ibrahim
Muharram – mourning of martyrdom of Imam Hussain
Milad-un-Nabi – celebration of Prophet Muhammad’s birth
Festivals emphasize charity, fasting, and community

notes.heading: Christian Festivals
points: Christmas – celebration of birth of Jesus Christ
Good Friday – remembrance of crucifixion of Jesus
Easter – celebration of resurrection of Jesus
Emphasis on faith, sacrifice, and renewal
Observed across India with regional variations

notes.heading: Sikh Festivals
points: Guru Nanak Jayanti – birth of Guru Nanak
Baisakhi – harvest festival and formation of Khalsa
Martyrdom days of Sikh Gurus
Emphasis on equality, service, and community
Celebrated with processions and langar

notes.heading: Buddhist Festivals
points: Buddha Purnima – birth, enlightenment, and death of Buddha
Asalha Puja – first sermon of Buddha
Kathina festival – offering of robes to monks
Emphasis on peace, meditation, and compassion
Observed in India and Buddhist countries

notes.heading: Jain Festivals
points: Mahavir Jayanti – birth of Lord Mahavira
Paryushana – period of fasting and forgiveness
Diwali – marks Nirvana of Mahavira
Emphasis on non-violence (Ahimsa)
Rituals include fasting and meditation

notes.heading: Seasonal and Harvest Festivals
points: Pongal – Tamil Nadu harvest festival
Onam – Kerala harvest festival
Bihu – Assam harvest festival
Lohri – Punjab winter harvest festival
Makar Sankranti – pan-India harvest celebration

notes.heading: Tribal Festivals
points: Hornbill Festival – Nagaland cultural festival
Chapchar Kut – Mizoram festival
Sarhul – Jharkhand tribal festival
Wangala – Meghalaya harvest festival
Celebrate nature, ancestors, and community life

notes.heading: Major Fairs of India
points: Kumbh Mela – largest religious gathering in the world
Pushkar Fair – Rajasthan cattle and camel fair
Sonepur Mela – Bihar livestock fair
Surajkund Mela – Haryana handicraft fair
Gangasagar Mela – West Bengal pilgrimage fair

notes.heading: Kumbh Mela
points: Held every 12 years at four locations: Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain, Nashik
One of the largest peaceful gatherings in the world
Based on Hindu mythology of nectar (Amrit)
UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage
Important pilgrimage for Hindus

notes.heading: Cultural Significance
points: Promote social harmony and unity
Preserve traditional arts, music, and dance
Encourage trade and local economy
Strengthen religious and cultural identity
Platform for cultural exchange

notes.heading: Economic Importance
points: Boost tourism industry
Support handicrafts and local artisans
Generate seasonal employment
Promote rural economy
Increase cultural exports

notes.heading: UPSC Importance
points: Frequently asked in Art & Culture section
Kumbh Mela and UNESCO tag are important
Matching festival-state questions are common
Tribal festivals are often asked in Prelims
Link between festivals and cultural geography is important

notes.heading: Overview
points: North-East India is one of the most culturally diverse regions of India
It includes 8 states: Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura, and Sikkim
Festivals are deeply connected with tribal traditions, agriculture, and nature worship
They reflect community life, oral traditions, and indigenous identity
Many festivals are now also promoted for tourism and cultural preservation

notes.heading: Assam – Major Festivals
points: Bihu – most important festival of Assam (three types: Rongali, Kongali, Bhogali)
Rongali Bihu – Assamese New Year and spring festival
Magh Bihu (Bhogali Bihu) – harvest and feast festival
Kongali Bihu – simple festival during crop growth stage
Ambubachi Mela – associated with Kamakhya Temple

notes.heading: Significance of Assam Festivals
points: Closely linked with agricultural cycles
Celebrates nature, fertility, and community bonding
Traditional dance (Bihu dance) and music are central
Strong participation of youth and rural communities
Blend of tribal and Hindu traditions

notes.heading: Nagaland – Major Festivals
points: Hornbill Festival – most famous cultural festival of Nagaland
Celebrates unity among different Naga tribes
Showcases traditional dance, music, crafts, and food
Held annually in Kisama Heritage Village
Named after the Hornbill bird, important in Naga culture

notes.heading: Significance of Nagaland Festivals
points: Preserves tribal identity and traditions
Promotes inter-tribal harmony
Boosts tourism and cultural exchange
Displays warrior traditions and folklore
Strong connection with nature and ancestry

notes.heading: Manipur – Major Festivals
points: Yaoshang – Manipuri version of Holi
Lai Haraoba – festival of local deities
Ningol Chakouba – family reunion festival
Cheiraoba – Meitei New Year
Raas Leela – devotional dance form

notes.heading: Significance of Manipur Festivals
points: Blend of Vaishnavism and indigenous traditions
Strong cultural importance of dance and music
Community bonding and family reunions
Religious devotion to local deities (Umang Lai)
Preservation of Manipuri classical dance tradition

notes.heading: Meghalaya – Major Festivals
points: Wangala Festival – harvest festival of Garo tribe
Shad Suk Mynsiem – Khasi thanksgiving festival
Behdeinkhlam – Jaintia festival for health and prosperity
Nongkrem Dance Festival – religious dance festival
A blend of tribal religion and nature worship

notes.heading: Significance of Meghalaya Festivals
points: Agriculture-based celebrations
Deep connection with nature and spirits
Traditional music, drums, and dance performances
Role of community elders and priests
Strong preservation of matrilineal culture

notes.heading: Mizoram – Major Festivals
points: Chapchar Kut – most important spring festival
Mim Kut – festival after maize harvest
Pawl Kut – harvest thanksgiving festival
Traditional dances like Cheraw (bamboo dance)
Community feasting and cultural performances

notes.heading: Significance of Mizoram Festivals
points: Closely linked with shifting cultivation (jhum)
Expression of gratitude for harvest
Strong role of music and dance
Community participation is central
Reflects Mizo cultural identity

notes.heading: Arunachal Pradesh – Major Festivals
points: Losar – Tibetan Buddhist New Year
Solung – Adi tribe harvest festival
Dree Festival – agricultural festival of Apatani tribe
Nyokum – worship of nature and spirits
Mopin – festival of Galo tribe

notes.heading: Significance of Arunachal Festivals
points: Mix of Buddhist and tribal traditions
Nature worship is central theme
Rituals for agricultural prosperity
Strong oral traditions and folklore
Community feasts and dances

notes.heading: Tripura – Major Festivals
points: Kharchi Puja – worship of 14 deities
Garia Puja – tribal festival for prosperity
Ker Puja – protection of community
Durga Puja – widely celebrated Hindu festival
Mix of tribal and Hindu traditions

notes.heading: Significance of Tripura Festivals
points: Blend of indigenous and Hindu practices
Agricultural and community protection rituals
Strong participation of tribal communities
Religious harmony among different groups
Cultural identity preservation

notes.heading: Sikkim – Major Festivals
points: Losar – Tibetan New Year
Saga Dawa – Buddha’s life events
Pang Lhabsol – worship of Mount Kanchenjunga
Losoong – harvest festival
Dasain (Dussehra) – Hindu influence

notes.heading: Significance of Sikkim Festivals
points: Strong influence of Tibetan Buddhism
Mountain worship and nature reverence
Blend of Hindu and Buddhist traditions
Community rituals and monasteries play key role
Cultural harmony among ethnic groups

notes.heading: Common Features of North-East Festivals
points: Strong connection with nature and agriculture
Community-based celebrations
Rich tribal dance and music traditions
Oral storytelling and folklore importance
Increasing role of tourism and cultural promotion

notes.heading: UPSC Importance
points: Frequently asked in Prelims (festival-state matching)
Hornbill Festival and Bihu are very important
Tribal festivals often appear in MCQs
Cultural geography of North-East is important
Useful for understanding India’s diversity in Mains answers
